children.name: Linxiavis
children.description: Linxiavis — a genus of sandgrouse in the family Pteroclidae.

children.name: Linxiavis inaquosus
children.description: Linxiavis inaquosus is an extinct species of sandgrouse known from a partial skeleton, found in the Late Miocene Liushu Formation at the edge of the Tibetan Plateau in Gansu Province of China. It is the most substantial and oldest record of crown Sandgrouse in China which adds to the rapidly growing avian fauna of the Liushu Formation.

children.name: Pterocles
children.description: Sandgrouse — medium-sized, ground-dwelling birds of arid and semi-arid regions. Despite their pigeon-like appearance, they are in their own order. Their most remarkable adaptation is the ability of males to absorb water in their belly feathers and carry it to their chicks at nests that can be kilometres from the nearest water source. Their cryptic plumage blends perfectly with desert sand and gravel.

children.name: Pterocles alchata
children.description:
The pin-tailed sandgrouse (Pterocles alchata) is a medium large bird in the sandgrouse family. It has a small, pigeon-like head and neck and a sturdy, compact body. It has long pointed wings, which are white underneath, a long tail and a fast direct flight. Flocks fly to watering holes at dawn. The call is a loud kattar-kattar. This gregarious species breeds on dry open treeless plains and similar habitats. Its nest is a ground scrape into which two or three cream-coloured eggs with cryptic markings are laid. Both sexes incubate the eggs.
The pin-tailed sandgrouse is about long. Its head and upperparts are yellowish-green. The underparts are white with a chestnut breast band separating the belly from the green neck. Sexes are somewhat similar, but the female is better camouflaged and has a shorter tail than the male. There are two subspecies; P. A. Alchata breeds in southern Europe and P. A. Caudacutus breeds in northwestern Africa, the Middle East and southeastern Asia. It is a partial migrant, with some Asian birds moving to the Middle East and northern Pakistan in winter. Males of the eastern race have duller underparts than the European birds, and the females have white, rather than yellow, wing coverts.

children.name: Pterocles orientalis
children.description:
The black-bellied sandgrouse (Pterocles orientalis) is a medium large bird in the sandgrouse family.
The nominate race breeds in Iberian Peninsula, Northwest Africa, the Canary Islands, Turkey, Iran, Cyprus and Palestine. The eastern form P. O. Arenarius (Pallas, 1775) is found in Kazakhstan, western China and northern Pakistan. It is a partial migrant, with central Asian birds moving to Pakistan and northern India in winter.

children.name: Pterocles exustus
children.description:
The chestnut-bellied sandgrouse or common sandgrouse (Pterocles exustus) is a species of sandgrouse. It is a sedentary and nomadic species that ranges from northern and central Africa and further east towards western and southern Asia. There are six recognized subspecies.
The chestnut-bellied sandgrouse is sexually dimorphic in plumage colouration and varies in overall plumage colouration between the six subspecies.

children.name: Pterocles gutturalis
children.description: The yellow-throated sandgrouse (Pterocles gutturalis) is a bird species of the family Pteroclidae. The species common name is derived from the male's distinctive yellow throat. It is found in arid and semi-arid environments and inhabits regions distributed across 10 different African countries. Two subspecies are accepted, P. G. Saturatior and P. G. Gutturalis. The yellow-throated sandgrouse is listed as Near Threatened in the South African regional assessment but regarded as Least Concerned globally.

children.name: Pterocles senegallus
children.description: The spotted sandgrouse (Pterocles senegallus) is a species of ground dwelling bird in the family Pteroclidae.

children.name: Pterocles quadatus
children.description: Found across sub-Saharan Africa from Mauritania to Ethiopia. Named for the four dark bands across the chest. Sandy-brown plumage provides excellent camouflage. Gregarious, forming large flocks at waterholes during the dry season.

children.name: Pterocles namaquensis
children.description: A striking sandgrouse of southern Africa. The male has a blue-grey head and breast with a brick-red throat patch. Found in the Namib Desert and arid regions of Botswana and South Africa. One of the most abundant sandgrouse in southern Africa.

children.name: Pterocles bicinctus
children.description: The double-banded sandgrouse (Pterocles bicinctus) is a species of predominantly terrestrial, or ground-dwelling (though not flightless), bird in the family Pteroclidae. It is found in arid parts of southern Africa.

children.name: Pterocles burchellii
children.description: A spotted sandgrouse from southern Africa.

children.name: Pterocles coronatus
children.description: The crowned sandgrouse (Pterocles coronatus) is a species of bird in the sandgrouse family, the Pteroclidae from North Africa and the Middle East.

children.name: Pterocles decoratus
children.description: The black-faced sandgrouse (Pterocles decoratus) is a species of ground-dwelling bird in the Pteroclidae family. It is a mainly sedentary bird found in East Africa, ranging from Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, Tanzania, and Uganda. It is a medium-sized bird which is well-adapted and well-camouflaged to life in arid environments. It is a dove-like bird due to its physical resemblance, particularly its small head, short legs, and pointed wings. It is listed as least concern on the IUCN Red List.

children.name: Pterocles lichtensteinii
children.description:
Lichtenstein's sandgrouse (Pterocles lichtensteinii) is a species of bird in the Pteroclidae family, which is named after Martin Lichtenstein. They are nomadic, mostly nocturnal birds, which drink before dawn and after dusk.
The species is found over a wide region, from near the equator in Kenya, through the Middle East to Afghanistan. In Africa it is besides found in Algeria, Chad, Djibouti, Egypt, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Libya, Mali, Mauritania, Morocco, Niger, Senegal, Somalia, Sudan and Uganda. In Asia it is also found in Iran, Iraq, Jordan, Oman, Pakistan, Palestine, Saudi Arabia, Israel, the United Arab Emirates and Yemen.

children.name: Pterocles personatus
children.description: The Madagascar sandgrouse (Pterocles personatus) is a species of bird in the family Pteroclidae.

children.name: Syrrhaptes
children.description: Pallas's sandgrouse — two species adapted to the high steppes and plateaus of Central Asia. They have feathered legs and feet adapted for walking on snow, and their chicks are born with a dense down that protects them from the cold. S. paradoxus is famous for irregular mass irruptions into western Europe.

children.name: Syrrhaptes paradoxus
children.description: Pallas's sandgrouse (Syrrhaptes paradoxus) is a medium to large bird in the sandgrouse family.

children.name: Syrrhaptes tibetanus
children.description: thumb|At Merak, Ladakh The Tibetan sandgrouse (Syrrhaptes tibetanus) is a large bird in the sandgrouse family.
